<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. V.|ACCORDING TO S. MATTHEW.|13}}</noinclude>him giue her a bil of diuorcement. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=33}}† But I say to you, whosoeuer shal dimisse his vvife, {{sup|‖}} excepting the cause of fornication, maketh her to {{sup|‖}} committe aduoutrie: And he that shal marie her that is dimissed, committeth aduoutrie.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=34}}† Agayne you haue heard that it vvas sayd to them of old, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 20, 7. Leu. 19, 11.''}}* Thou shalt not committe periurie: but thou shalt performe thy othes to our Lord. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=35}}† But I say to you {{sup|‖}} not to sweare at al: neither by heauen, because it is the throne of God: neither by the earth, because it is the foote-stole of his feete: neither by Hierusalē, because it is the citie of the great King. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=36}}† Neither shalt thou sweare by thy head, because thou canst not make one heare vvhite or blacke. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=37}}† Let your talke be, yea, yea: no, no: and that vvhich is ouer & aboue these, is of euil.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=38}}† You haue heard that it vvas sayd, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 21, 24.''}}* An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=39}}† But I say to you {{sup|‖}} not to resist euil: but if one strike thee on thy right cheeke, turne to him also the other: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=40}}† and to him that vvil contend vvith thee in iudgment, and take away thy cote, let goe thy cloke also vnto him, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=41}}† and vvhosoeuer vvil force thee one mile, goe vvith him other tvvayne. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=42}}† He that asketh of thee, giue to him: and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 15, 7.''}}* to him that vvould borovv of thee, turne not avvay.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=43}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the friday after Ashwensday.}}You haue heard that it vvas sayd, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Leu. 19, 18.''}}* Thou shalt loue thy neighbour, and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ So taught the Pharisees, not the Law.}}∷ hate thine enemie. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=44}}† But I say to you, loue your enemies, doe good to them that hate you: and pray for them that persecute and abuse you: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=45}}† that you may be the children of your father vvhich is in heauen, vvho maketh his sunne to rise vpon good & bad, and rayneth vpon iust & {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ We see then that the temporal prosperitie of persons and countries is no signe of better men or truer religion.}}∷ vniust. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=46}}† For if you loue them that loue you, vvhat revvard shal you haue? do not also the Publicans this? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=47}}† And if you salute your brethren only, vvhat do you more? do not also the heathen this? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=48}}† Be you perfect therfore, as also your heauenly father is perfect.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. V.}}}}

''10. For iustice.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=False Martyrs.}}Heretikes and other malefactours sometime suffer willingly and stoutly: but they are not blessed, because they suffer not for iustice. For (sayth S. Aug.) they can not suffer for iustice, that haue deuided the Churche. and, where sound fayth or charitie is not, there cannot be iustice. ''Cont. ep. Parm. li. 1. c. 9. Ep. 50. Psal. 34. Conc. 2''. And so by this scripture are excluded al false Martyrs, as S. Augustine often declareth, and S. Cypr. ''de Vnit. Eccl. nu. 8''.

''12. Reward.''] In Latin and Greeke the word {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Merces. ''Μισθὸς.''}}signifieth very wages and hire dewe for workes, and so presupposeth a meritorious deede.<noinclude>{{rh||B iij|''15. The''}}</noinclude>
